mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring additional conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by >0.3pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales exceeding 0.5% in two months indicate broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by >0.5% in 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing production below 100 (INDPRO) during a supply-side slowdown correlates with reduced corporate output capacity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as earnings growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.5% signals rising inflation that triggers Fed tightening expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises by >0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly payroll gains exceeding 150,000 (PAYEMS) indicate robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 150,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth below 1.5% annualized (GDPC1) during late-cycle expansion periods correlates with slowing economic momentum, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth is below 1.5% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in manufacturing production (INDPRO) and GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 0.5% and 0.2% respectively over three months signal economic contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through reduced corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and GDPC1 both decline > 0.5% and > 0.2% respectively in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO and GDPC1 decline by >0.5% and >0.2% respectively in 3 months.
